stories.text: Also Kokua Molokaʻi is an educational program designed by Learning Endeavors to inspire a deeper connection with the ʻāina through meaningful watershed experiences. Kokua Molokaʻi provides camps and teacher workshops to strengthen the network of stewards who care for the land and water. We deliver experiential opportunities for keiki and kumu alike, embracing cultural A legendary kahuna and kaula who lived during the 1500s. Often referred to in songs, chants, and stories, Lani Kaula is one of the most famous places on Molokaʻi. Caring for this place, tending to the trees, sharing the ike and providing stewardship is Uncle Bobby Elkayne. He, with members of the Molokaʻi community, have perpetuated The legacy of the sacred Kukui Grove. According to history, at one time the Kukui trees blanketed the Ahupuaʻa of Keopuka and over the eastern slopes of Molokaʻi. There, the winds first greet the island, bringing the rains that nourish the lush eastern hillsides and mountains of Molokaʻi. From there, we traveled to the Kaʻamola Ahupuaʻa and visited Kaupapaloio This calopatch is being restored to a glorious network of loʻi with fish, taro, and waterways that open up to a fish pond. This restoration project is led by the non-profit organization Kaipumakani Cultural Heritage Center. We learned that this is a loʻipunawai within ainawai. This means a spring-fed loʻi in a natural coastal wetland area. The spring fedloʻi serves as a filter to prevent excess nutrients from eroding and entering the ocean, which can harm the coral reef. The Kokua Molokaʻi approach develops individual capacity, builds stewardship networks, and deepens knowledge of place, all while having fun. Join us for an enriching watershed experience during our upcoming expeditions for youth or teacher workshops. Very, very beautiful.

stories.headline: Survey finds survival sex among female wildfire survivors
stories.summary: A Tagnawa survey found one in six female survivors felt forced into survival sex after the 2023 wildfires, and calls to Women Helping Women more than doubled.
stories.text: A survey by Tagnawa published in The Guardian, a Filipino feminist disaster response organization, found that one in six female survivors felt forced to engage in survival sex for basic necessities, such as food, clothing, and housing after the 2023 wildfires. Immigrant women felt particularly unsafe. Some fire survivors felt trapped in violent relationships with nowhere to go. Calls to women helping women more than doubled. Anecdotal reports from key experts suggests that intrafamilial violence among survivors remains high to this day.

stories.text: Dr. Gerhard Konig, the Maui doctor accused of attempting to murder his wife on the Pali Trail on Oahu, and his wife, both appeared virtually for their divorce hearing yesterday to try to keep their divorce case private. stories.headline: Dori Booth named Hawaiʻi's first State Fire Marshal in decades
stories.summary: Governor Josh Green appointed Dori Booth to revive the State Fire Marshal role, vacant for nearly 46 years, to strengthen statewide fire protection after the 2023 Maui wildfires.
stories.text: Governor Josh Green has appointed Dorey Booth as Hawaiʻi's new state fire marshal, reviving a role vacant for nearly 46 years. The position was eliminated in 1979 with fire responsibilities being handed off to the counties. Booth's appointment will centralize and strengthen statewide fire protection efforts and follows calls for statewide coordination after the 2023 Maui wildfires. Her role marks a shift toward rebuilding Hawaiʻi's fire safety infrastructure.
